curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8820-1/ (scans; the buggy is pages 3-6, steps 1-13; pages 7-10 are the alternate model, and page 1's left half adds the 8720 motor to it)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column runs down at a slant to an 8-tooth gear that slides the steering rack across, and the rack's ends swing the two steering arms.
functions.source: book: steps 3 (steering arms), 4 (rack and its holder), 7 (steering wheel on its 6-long column, inset); the cover blueprint draws the front wheels turned

functions.does: The rear wheels ride on a swinging arm: two 1x6 bricks, one each side, pivot on a 10-long axle under the seat and carry the rear wheels on axle pins, joined at the back by an 8-long axle that the shock absorber pushes down, so the rear wheels rise and fall together.
functions.source: book: step 5 (shock absorber between a 6-long axle and an 8-long axle; the inset's arrows show it squeezing), step 11 (the 10-long pivot axle pushed through the arms), steps 12-13 (rear wheels)
functions.note: how far the arm can swing is set by the shock absorber's travel; its cylinder swings a little on its top axle as the arm moves

functions.does: The shock absorber's spring pushes the rear wheels back down.
functions.skip: a spring only matters under gravity or force

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely, each on its own axle pin; there's no drive.
functions.note: rolling shouldn't swing the rear arm
